name: Earth-Moon L2
story: The Lagrange point about 61,000 km behind the Moon as seen from Earth — the gravitational saddle where Earth, Moon, and centrifugal forces balance. The Moon always sits between the spacecraft and Earth, so direct comms are impossible — but a satellite parked here in a halo orbit AROUND L2 has line-of-sight to BOTH the lunar farside AND Earth. That's how China landed Chang'e 4 on the farside in 2019: the Queqiao relay satellite, parked in a halo around Earth-Moon L2, bridges every command and image.
comparison: About 1/6th the distance from Earth to the Moon. Without a relay at L2, the entire lunar farside is a comms blackout — every spacecraft that ever landed there has needed one.

firsts.label: Queqiao — first operational Earth-Moon L2 relay (China)
